tone_statements.citation: DiCanio, Christian & Richard Hatcher. 2025. Prosody without intonation. Talk presented at the 3rd Tone and Intonation Conference (TAI 2025), Herrsching, Germany. Slides, 38 pp.https://www.acsu.buffalo.edu/~cdicanio/pdfs/TAI_2025_DiCanio_Hatcher.pdf
tone_statements.quote: Tone in Triqui • Nine lexical tones /5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 43, 32, 31, 13/ (5 = high) • No tonally-unmarked syllables/morphemes. • Open syllables, but word-final codas /ʔ, h/. • Mostly disyllabic word structure, but tone on non-final syllables is often predictable.
tone_statements.summary: 9 lexical tones incl. 5 levels (/5 4 3 2 1/ + /43 32 31 13/); all syllables toned; leftward spread of /4/; heavy grammatical tone; no declination, no boundary tones.

tone_statements.quote: There are nine contrastive tones in uninflected words in the language, though additional tones occur in certain inflected forms. Stress is fixed, non-contrastive, and obligatory in stem-final syllables. ... Contour tones freely surface on final open syllables, though tone /45/ surfaces only with a coda /ɦ/. ... Only level tones may surface on syllables with a /ʔ/ coda. ... Here and elsewhere, /5/ reflects the highest tone and /1/ the lowest.

tone_statements.summary: Nine tones (level /4 3 2 1/, contours /45 13 43 32 31/) in [+/-upper] registers; TBU = mora, stressed stem-final syllable bimoraic; 'No floating tones' principle; extra tones in inflected forms.

tone_statements.quote: El idioma triqui tiene nueve tonos que sirven para distinguir el significado de la palabra. Estos tonos son cambios de la tonía de la voz. ... Escala de los tonos El super alto (5) bbéj ‘petate’ El alto (4) bbé ‘pelo’ El medio (3) nne ‘arado’, ‘se sienta’ El bajo (2) nnè ‘mentir’ El super bajo (1) nnè ‘desnudo’ El descendente alto (43) chée ‘mi padre’ El descendente (32) nnee ‘agua’ El descendente bajo (31) nneè ‘carne’ El ascendente (13) yyèej ‘sí’
tone_statements.translation: The Triqui language has nine tones that serve to distinguish the meaning of the word. These tones are changes in the pitch of the voice. ... Scale of the tones: super high (5) bbéj 'mat'; high (4) bbé 'hair'; mid (3) nne 'plough', 'sits'; low (2) nnè 'to lie'; super low (1) nnè 'naked'; high falling (43) chée 'my father'; falling (32) nnee 'water'; low falling (31) nneè 'meat'; rising (13) yyèej 'yes'.
tone_statements.locator: p.9 sec. III 'Los tonos' and p.10 'Escala de los tonos' (page numbers are footers)
tone_statements.summary: Literacy primer: nine tones (5 levels, 3 falling, 1 rising) with minimal pairs; orthography ´=high, `=low, unmarked=mid, double vowels for contours; tone also marks person and future (grave accent).

tone_statements.citation: DiCanio, Christian & Richard Hatcher. 2018. On the non-universality of intonation: Evidence from Triqui. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America 144(3_Supplement): 1941 (meeting abstract). doi:10.1121/1.5068494
tone_statements.quote: We present results from three field experiments with 11 speakers where we investigated information structure and prosody in Itunyoso Triqui, an Otomanguean language (Mexico). Itunyoso Triqui possesses nine lexical tones (/4, 3, 2, 1, 43, 32, 31, 13, 45/), fixed final stress, and contrastive phonation type. ... In experiment 3, we investigated F0 declination in sentences consisting of only level tones and found no F0 change across utterances. The results from these experiments suggest that Itunyoso Triqui does not use F0 to encode information structure or prosodic boundaries.
tone_statements.summary: Nine lexical tones (4 level, 5 contour) plus fixed final stress; F0 study finds no intonational use of pitch. Authors' 2018 slides: tones contrast on final syllables, no pitch accents/boundary tones.

tone_statements.citation: DiCanio, Christian T. 2012. Cross-linguistic perception of Itunyoso Trique tone. Journal of Phonetics 40(5): 672-688. doi:10.1016/j.wocn.2012.05.003 (author PDF:https://www.acsu.buffalo.edu/~cdicanio/pdfs/DiCanio_2012_perception.pdf)
tone_statements.quote: There are nine contrastive tones in Itunyoso Trique: four level tones and ﬁve contour tones. Unlike many East-Asian and Southeast Asian tonal languages, most words in Itunyoso Trique are polysyllabic. Contrastive tone occurs on every syllable in the word, but the full set of tonal contrasts may only occur on the ﬁnal syllables of lexical roots. Moreover, these nine different tones are unevenly distributed in ﬁnal syllables of three possible rime shapes: long vowels without a coda (/V7/), short vowels with a voiced glottal fricative coda (/V9/), and short vowels followed by a coda glottal stop (/V /).

tone_statements.summary: 9 lexical tones: 4 level + 3 falling (/43 32 31/) + 2 rising (/13 45/); every syllable tone-bearing, full set only on root-final syllables; distribution by rime type (Vː, Vɦ, Vʔ).

The 2008 Berkeley dissertation (295 pp, Glottolog's top-ranked phonology for this languoid) says the same at p.20 ('having both final stress and a rich tone inventory'), and DiCanio 2014 and 2022 restate it as 'stem-final'/'root-final' stress with final-syllable lengthening independent of utterance position and focus. Nothing found contradicts the classification. sources.quote: there are phonetic correlates to the final syllable prominence. Consonants and vowels in final syllables are noticeably longer [...] Since this is the position of stress in Trique [...] they result from a system of final prominence independent from tone.

sources.citation: DiCanio, Christian Thomas. 2008. The Phonetics and Phonology of San Martín Itunyoso Trique. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley. 295 pp.
sources.quote: p.20: 'Itunyoso Trique is prosodically complex, having both final stress and a rich tone inventory (9 tones). There are strong motivations for positing stress in the language apart from tone. The main evidence is the many asymmetries in the distribution of tone, consonants, and vowels... While word-final syllables license all segmental and autosegmental contrasts in the language, penultimate and antepenultimate syllables permit far fewer contrasts.' p.30: 'The similar patterns among the three dialects suggest that final stress is a shared feature in the Trique languages.'
sources.note: The only full phonology of the language (Glottolog listed by Glottolog as a phonology, 295 pp); §2.2 p.20 states final stress and gives the distributional evidence behind the JIPA summary; second independent locator for the record.

sources.citation: DiCanio, Christian. 2022. The evolution of tonally conditioned allomorphy in Triqui: evidence from spontaneous speech corpora. Linguistics Vanguard (aop). doi:10.1515/lingvan-2021-0093 (author preprint)
sources.quote: 'Root-final syllables are accentually prominent and many phonological contrasts may only occur in this position... In addition, root-final syllables are phonetically longer than non-final syllables regardless of the position of the word in the utterance or focus condition (DiCanio 2010; DiCanio and Hatcher 2018).' Later: 'since stem-final syllables are stressed and carry heavy functional load in the language, stem-final syllables are often phonologically stable.'
sources.note: States the stress domain explicitly (root-/stem-final, enclitics outside; lengthening independent of utterance position and focus) -- fills the record's not yet coded domain field.

sources.citation: DiCanio, Christian & Ryan Bennett. 2018 (preprint; published 2020 in Gussenhoven & Chen eds., The Oxford Handbook of Language Prosody). Prosody in Mesoamerican languages.
sources.quote: 'stress has been explored instrumentally in a few Mixtecan languages (Ixpantepec Nieves Mixtec (Carroll 2015), Southeastern Nochixtlán Mixtec (McKendry 2013), and Itunyoso Triqui (DiCanio 2008; 2010)). In each of these languages, the main correlate of stress is acoustic duration.'

sources.citation: DiCanio, Christian. 2014. Triqui tonal coarticulation and contrast preservation in tonal phonology. Proceedings of the Workshop on the Sound Systems of Mexico and Central America (SSMCA), Yale. (author PDF)
sources.quote: 'In addition to lexical tone, IT possesses stem-final stress. Final syllables are phonetically longer than non-final syllables and more phonological contrasts are realized on final syllables as well (DiCanio, 2008, 2010).'
sources.note: One-line restatement 'IT possesses stem-final stress' with duration evidence; corroborates domain = stem.
